  df1 <- k
  df2 <- N - p
  
  if (df2 <= 0) return(0)
  
  # Critical value from central F distribution (one-tailed test)
  F_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- df2 * R2 / (1 - R2)
  
  # Power from noncentral F distribution
  power <- 1 - pf(F_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum N that achieves target power

# Sample size calculation for testing H0: R² = 0 vs H1: R² > 0
# Parameters
alpha <- 0.05           # significance level (two-tailed)
target_power <- 0.90    # desired power
k <- 3                  # number of predictors
p <- k + 1              # total parameters (intercept + 3 predictors)
r_multiple <- 0.30      # anticipated multiple correlation
R2_alt <- r_multiple^2  # anticipated R-squared under alternative
R2_null <- 0            # null hypothesis R-squared

# For noncentral F test:
# Test statistic: F = [R²/(1-R²)] × [(N-p)/k]
# Under H1, F ~ F_noncentral(df1=k, df2=N-p, lambda)
# where lambda = (N-p) × R²/(1-R²) × [1 + something...actually let me recalculate]
# The noncentrality parameter is: λ = (N-p) × R²/(1-R²)

# Two-tailed test: reject if F > F_crit(α/2, k, N-p) [actually one-tailed on upper]
# For R² test, it's one-tailed: reject if F > F_crit(α, k, N-p)

# Critical F-value depends on sample size, so we need to iterate
# Power = P(F > F_crit(α, k, N-p) | λ = (N-p) × R²/(1-R²))

# Function to compute power given sample size
compute_power <- function(N, alpha, k, R2, p) {
  df1 <- k
  df2 <- N - p
  
  # Critical value from central F distribution
  F_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- df2 * R2 / (1 - R2)
  
  # Power from noncentral F distribution
  power <- 1 - pf(F_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum N that achieves target power
# Start with a reasonable guess
N_min <- p + 1
N_max <- 500

# Binary search or linear search
for (N in N_min:N_max) {
  power <- compute_power(N, alpha, k, R2_alt, p)
  if (power >= target_power) {
    N_target <- N
    power_target <- power
    break
  }
}

# Verify the previous N
N_previous <- N_target - 1
power_previous <- compute_power(N_previous, alpha, k, R2_alt, p)

# Display results
cat("Study Design: Linear Regression R² Significance Test\n")
cat("Parameters:\n")
